eeprom_layout_ref.reference_note: EZ-USB FX2LP serial-EEPROM boot formats as documented in the public device datasheet and technical reference manual. Offsets and field meanings are transcribed from public documentation only; no value here is derived from any device dump.
eeprom_layout_ref.endianness_note: Identifier fields (VID/PID/DID) are stored little-endian (LSB first). C2 firmware data-record length and address words are stored big-endian (MSB first).

boot_formats.C0: Identifier-only image: overrides VID/PID/DID and the configuration byte; no 8051 firmware is loaded from EEPROM.
boot_formats.C2: Firmware image: identifier header followed by one or more code/data records loaded into internal RAM, terminated by a final record that releases the 8051 from reset.

fields.name: boot_config_byte
fields.description: Leading boot-configuration byte that selects the EEPROM boot format (0xC0 identifier-only, 0xC2 firmware load). Any other value means the controller ignores the EEPROM.

fields.name: vid
fields.description: USB Vendor ID override word (LSB at 0x01, MSB at 0x02).

fields.name: pid
fields.description: USB Product ID override word (LSB at 0x03, MSB at 0x04).

fields.name: did
fields.description: USB Device release / Device ID override word (LSB at 0x05, MSB at 0x06).

fields.name: config_byte
fields.description: Configuration byte holding the I2C bus-speed select bit and the disconnect (DISCON) control bit as defined in the public datasheet.

fields.name: data_record_length
fields.description: First C2 firmware data-record length word (MSB first). The high bit of this word on the final record flags the end of the record list.

fields.name: data_record_address
fields.description: First C2 firmware data-record load address word (MSB first): the internal-RAM destination for the following payload bytes.

fields.name: data_record_payload
fields.description: Payload bytes of the first C2 firmware data record. Records repeat (length, address, payload) until the final record is reached.

fields.name: final_record
fields.description: Terminating C2 record: a single payload byte written to the reset-control register at 0xE600 to release the 8051 core from reset once all firmware records are loaded.

session_phases.boundary_basis: The dense startup sequence ends at frame 4710 (9.344725 s, opcode 0x08). Frame 4720 (9.371560 s, opcode 0x01) starts a 194-command 0x01 run lasting to 19.141799 s, followed by recurring mixed-opcode bursts.

phases.name: init
phases.pattern: Sparse 0x00/0x02 opening, short 0x01 cadence, a dense tag-0 0x09 run, then dense tag-1 0x08 and mixed 0x08-0x11 sequences.

phases.name: steady
phases.pattern: A roughly 20 Hz tag-0 0x01 baseline is interrupted by recurring mixed tag-1 0x08/0x09/0x0a/0x0b sequences and tag-0 0x04/0x05/0x09 activity.
phases.stationarity_boundary: The steady label describes the post-init regime, not a stationary process. Burst spacing is irregular, and distinct 0x08-heavy episodes occur near 83.79, 90.54, and 94.77 seconds.

observations: Opcodes 0x00, 0x01, 0x02, 0x04, and 0x05 occur only with tag 0x0000 in this capture.
Opcodes 0x0b, 0x0c, 0x0d, 0x0f, 0x10, and 0x11 occur only with tag 0x0001 in this capture.
Opcode 0x08 is strongly associated with tag 0x0001 (507/522); opcode 0x0a is strongly associated with tag 0x0001 (79/80).
Opcode 0x09 spans both tags (1028 tag-0 and 127 tag-1) and therefore is not a tag discriminator.
The 833 tag-1 OUT and 833 tag-1 IN counts are equal, while tag-0 has 290 more OUT than IN payloads. This is a stream-level correlation only and does not prove the tag's semantic role.

candidate_transition.relationship: volatile firmware load followed by USB renumeration

timeline.evidence: First traffic for USB address 8, followed by its DEVICE descriptor.

timeline.interpretation: CPUCS reset released after first load

timeline.note: Included to make the gap between the two 0xA0 load stages explicit; request semantics are not asserted here.

timeline.evidence: USB address 8 is silent after the final CPUCS completion; the next frame is a same-bus hub status-change interrupt.
timeline.boundary: USBPcap contains no explicit device-disconnect record, so the disconnect is inferred rather than directly observed.

timeline.evidence: First traffic for new USB address 9, followed by its DEVICE descriptor.

usb_renumeration_timeline.interpretation: The observed 0x3923:0x7317 loader at address 8 receives two 0xA0 memory-load/readback bursts bracketed by CPUCS writes, then goes silent after the final CPUCS release. A hub change follows and 0x3923:0x744f appears at address 9. This supports, but does not independently prove, a loader-to-runtime renumeration.
usb_renumeration_timeline.boundary: VID/PID descriptors, requests, payload bytes, frame numbers, and times are observed. CPUCS meaning follows the public Cypress FX2 0xE600 convention; the disconnect and identity continuity across addresses are candidate inferences.

source.packet_definition: payload-bearing USBPcap records only; submit/completion records without usb.capdata are excluded

measurement_method.inter_arrival: delta between capture timestamps of consecutive payload-bearing records on the same endpoint
measurement_method.entropy: Shannon entropy in bits per byte; it describes captured byte distributions, not ADC effective number of bits
measurement_method.word_probe: non-semantic structural probe using four-byte words; both endian interpretations were tested

length_bytes.histogram_encoding: Each key is an occurrence count and its array contains every payload length having that count.

inter_arrival_s.interpretation: The large all-gap mean is idle-session dominated. Active bursts have an approximately 1.73 ms median with an approximately 10 ms upper cadence.

ep06_out.boundary_observation: The 512/2000-byte modes look like host transfer segmentation, but this capture alone does not establish whether EP06 carries samples, setup tables, FPGA data, or another vendor-defined payload.

length_bytes.histogram_encoding: Each key is an occurrence count and its array contains every payload length having that count.

inter_arrival_s.interpretation: Active arrivals are variable rather than a single fixed packet period; long gaps represent separate idle or acquisition intervals.

first_window_entropy_and_repetition.interpretation: The only repeated 16/32/64-byte starts are 51 payloads that remain one repeated four-byte value for the entire payload. Those values also occur tens of thousands of times away from payload starts, so they are more consistent with flat data runs than unique packet magic.

four_byte_periodicity.interpretation: A four-byte, big-endian-aligned numeric representation is strongly visible. This is a packing observation, not confirmation that each word is an ADC sample.

channel_stride_probe.method: Within each payload, decode structural big-endian words shifted right by seven and compare absolute differences at word lags 1 through 16.
channel_stride_probe.result: No periodic local minimum identifies a round-robin channel count from 2 through 16. Lag 1 is smoothest.
channel_stride_probe.limitation: Channels carrying correlated or identical signals could hide interleaving; a known per-channel stimulus is required.

urb_boundary_continuity.definition: consecutive EP84 payloads separated by at most one second
urb_boundary_continuity.interpretation: Active payload boundaries are as smooth as interior word boundaries, and no first-word length field is visible. USB payloads therefore look like transport fragments of a continuous word stream rather than self-contained blocks with an obvious four-byte header.

hypotheses.statement: EP84 is a continuous stream of four-byte, big-endian-aligned numeric words; USB payload boundaries normally do not reset the represented sequence.
support: 294 of 294 payload lengths are multiples of four.
The fourth byte is always 0x00 or 0x80, so every big-endian word has seven zero low bits.
Big-endian shifted values are smooth both inside payloads and across active payload boundaries.
Little-endian interpretation lacks the fixed low-bit structure and has much larger adjacent differences.
would_falsify: A known stimulus decodes coherently only with a different byte phase or endian order.
New captures show insertion/deletion at four-byte boundaries or non-0x00/0x80 fourth bytes during normal acquisition.
Firmware or protocol evidence identifies these bytes as non-numeric records.

hypotheses.statement: Each four-byte slot may contain a big-endian 24-bit value in bytes 0..2 plus one auxiliary bit at byte 3 bit 7; that bit could instead be the least-significant bit of a 25-bit fixed-point value.
support: Bytes 0..2 vary while byte 3 is restricted to 0x00/0x80 over all 845949 words.
The layout is compatible with three value bytes plus a one-bit tag, flag, or extra precision bit.
counterevidence: A conventional 24-bit value left-justified in 32 bits would normally have byte 3 equal to 0x00, but 348400 words (41.19 percent) have 0x80.
Treating bit 7 as numeric produces a smooth 25-bit structural sequence, so the capture does not separate a flag from numeric precision.
would_falsify: If bit 7 changes as required by numeric least-significant-bit continuity under a calibrated ramp, the separate auxiliary-bit interpretation is falsified.
If bit 7 follows an independent channel/status condition while bytes 0..2 track a known stimulus, the 25-bit numeric interpretation is falsified.
A calibrated transfer function with more or fewer than 24 value bits would falsify the 24-bit-value interpretation.

hypotheses.statement: EP84 may be a boundary-agnostic stream of tightly packed three-byte samples spanning USB payloads.
support: USB payload boundaries need not coincide with sample boundaries, so individual lengths need not be divisible by three.
The complete EP84 byte count, 3383796, is divisible by three.
counterevidence: All 294 payload lengths are divisible by four.
Length residues modulo three are exactly 98 each for residues 0, 1, and 2.
A stable low-entropy byte lane repeats every four bytes from the first byte of every payload.
would_falsify: A known ramp or tone that decodes continuously in four-byte words but not as a concatenated three-byte stream.
Independent captures that preserve the four-byte phase while total byte count is not divisible by three.

hypotheses.statement: The observed EP84 sequence behaves like one scalar word stream (channel stride one word/four bytes), with no detectable 2..16-channel round-robin stride.
support: Lag 1 has the smallest median and p90 adjacent difference.
Lag differences rise without periodic minima through lag 16.
would_falsify: Driving exactly one physical channel produces a response only in every Nth word for N greater than one.
A repeated lane-specific channel identifier or a robust lag-N minimum appears across independent stimuli.

hypotheses.statement: Two or more channels may still be interleaved at a fixed word stride, but correlated inputs in this session conceal the stride.
support: The capture has no documented per-channel stimulus, so correlated channel values cannot be excluded.
counterevidence: No lag from 2 through 16 is smoother than lag 1.
No channel marker has been identified in the four-byte slots.
would_falsify: Independent single-channel stimulation changes consecutive words uniformly rather than one residue class modulo N.
A device configuration proving one active channel while preserving the same stream structure.

hypotheses.statement: EP84 payloads are mostly headerless USB transport fragments aligned to four-byte values, not protocol blocks with a per-payload header.
support: Across active payload boundaries, median/p90 deltas match interior deltas.
Neither endian interpretation of the first u32 equals payload length in any payload.
The two repeated first words occur 74744 and 74704 times away from payload starts and fill 51 entire payloads, so they are not unique start magic.
Per-position entropy in the first 64 bytes repeats by byte lane every four bytes rather than showing a distinct leading field.
would_falsify: A stable magic, counter, timestamp, flags, checksum, or length field is found at every logical block start and validated across captures.
Removing a fixed leading field produces better cross-payload numeric continuity than decoding from byte zero.
Logical block starts are shown to differ from USB payload boundaries and carry a validated in-band header.

hypotheses.statement: An unrecognized variable or in-band block header may exist even though no fixed per-USB-payload header is visible.
support: A single passive capture cannot exclude headers that occur only at logical blocks inside the stream.
counterevidence: Observed USB boundaries preserve numeric continuity.
No fixed magic or first-u32 length relation is present.
would_falsify: A complete known-stimulus decode accounts for every four-byte word as continuous values across all acquisition intervals without skipped fields.
Multiple captures show no invariant/counter/checksum structure at independently identified acquisition starts.

hypotheses.statement: EP06 is a host-to-device bulk data-plane transport whose 512/2000-byte modes are transfer segmentation rather than an identified semantic frame format.
support: 416 of 417 payloads are divisible by eight and use only 512 or 2000 bytes.
The active cadence differs from EP84 and includes tightly spaced records.
would_falsify: A stable command opcode/length/checksum grammar explains EP06 payloads and predicts device responses.
Known experiments identify the payload as firmware/configuration upload rather than acquisition data.

meaning.candidate: supported by repeated capture-level structure but not semantically validated
meaning.hypothesis: plausible interpretation requiring controlled experiments or firmware/protocol corroboration

required_next_experiments: Capture zero, positive/negative DC, and ramp stimuli while recording engineering values and active channel count.
Toggle one channel at a time to test residue classes at candidate word strides.
Repeat captures at multiple requested sample counts to distinguish logical blocks from USB transfer segmentation.
Correlate byte 3 bit 7 with numeric transitions and known status/channel changes.
Validate signedness, scale, offset, and any checksum/counter against independent device behavior before declaring samples decoded.

field_under_test.frame_layout: BE u16 tag | BE u16 frame_len | BE u16 body_len | u8 type | u8 opcode_or_status | payload

layout_validation.rule: frame_len equals the complete USB bulk payload length and body_len equals frame_len - 4

out_type_by_tag.notable_equality: For each tag, the type-0x01 EP01 OUT count exactly equals the EP81 IN count: tag 0 has 2601 and tag 1 has 833.

type_0x00_detail.response_semantics: candidate response-less/one-way form; no claim beyond this capture

ordered_response_evidence.method: Remove the 290 type-0x00 OUT frames, then compare the tag sequence of the remaining 3434 OUT frames with the tag sequence of all 3434 IN frames in capture order.
ordered_response_evidence.interpretation: The IN frame mirrors the corresponding FIFO-ordered type-0x01 OUT tag. The 47 apparent adjacent tag mismatches occur when two requests are outstanding, so immediate adjacency is not a safe pairing rule.

correlation: 0x09 occurs with both tags (1028 tag 0x0000, 127 tag 0x0001), so tag is not merely an opcode-family bit.

temporal_shape.interpretation: Tag 0x0000 dominates long baseline runs, while tag 0x0001 is concentrated in shorter, faster bursts. Both values repeat and are not unique per transaction.

hypothesis.primary: The first u16 is a two-valued logical message-class or channel selector that is copied from a response-bearing EP01 request into its FIFO-corresponding EP81 response.
hypothesis.tag_0x0000_role: Baseline/control-polling-oriented class in this session; it carries all observed type-0x00 candidate one-way traffic and the long 0x01/0x09 runs.
hypothesis.tag_0x0001_role: Burst-oriented class in this session; it is strongly associated with the 0x08 and 0x0a families and exclusively carries the observed 0x0b-0x11 subset listed above.
hypothesis.why_not_transaction_id: Only two values occur, identical values repeat for runs as long as 771 requests, and the field correlates strongly with opcode and burst class. It can assist response association but is not a unique transaction identifier.
hypothesis.why_not_response_flag: Both values occur in OUT and IN. The separate type byte, not the tag alone, cleanly accounts for the 290 OUT frames without an IN counterpart.
hypothesis.semantic_limit: The capture proves framing, counts, ordering, and correlation. It does not distinguish among channel ID, subsystem selector, command namespace, priority class, or another vendor-defined role.

usb_stream_tag_hypothesis.key_conclusion: 0x0000 and 0x0001 are best treated as echoed logical class/channel tags, not lengths or unique transaction numbers: every type-0x01 OUT tag is mirrored in FIFO order by an IN tag (3434/3434), while tag 0x0000 marks long baseline/one-way activity and tag 0x0001 marks shorter command bursts.
usb_stream_tag_hypothesis.boundary: Single observational session with no controlled stimulus, host call trace, or device firmware symbol map. Opcode and tag names are intentionally not promoted to vendor semantics.

source.payload_accounting: usb.data_len on successful device-to-host bulk completions

methodology.active_burst_rule: At least two payload completions in a segment; split segments wherever consecutive payload completions are more than 1.0 s apart.
methodology.active_duration_rule: Elapsed time from the first through the last payload completion in each active burst.
methodology.sustained_rate_rule: Active-burst payload bytes divided by the sum of active-burst completion spans.
methodology.peak_rate_rule: Maximum payload bytes completed in any forward rolling window, divided by the full nominal window width.

transfer_status.note: Canceled zero-length completions occur when queued reads are canceled after segment termination and are excluded from byte/rate calculations.

possible_fifo_underrun_indicators.long_internal_gap_rule: Within an active burst, inter-payload gap >= 100 ms.
possible_fifo_underrun_indicators.assessment: No direct USB-level FIFO-underrun indicator is present. Every >=100 ms internal gap is followed by a large successful completion, which is compatible with host scheduling, queued-read batching, or FIFO accumulation; capture timing alone cannot distinguish those causes from a data-generation pause.

sample_rate_envelopes.assumption: Ideal upper envelope: each simultaneous N-channel scan consumes exactly N * 3 payload bytes, with no framing, metadata, padding, loss, or host/device overhead.

usb_throughput_hypothesis.boundary: Estimate only from this capture; no device-rated throughput or sample-rate specifications were used or inferred. USBPcap completion density is not a guaranteed bus-rate or device-limit measurement.
